paul.name: Paul
paul.role: Writer who corrects the Thessalonians and asks for prayer
paul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
paul.importance: Paul thanks the Thessalonians for growing faith in suffering. He asks them not to be shaken by a letter said to come from him. He tells them to withdraw from brothers who will not work. He signs the greeting with his own hand as the sign in every letter.
paul.connections: He writes with Silvanus and Timothy. He calls the readers brothers.

silas.name: Silvanus
silas.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Timothy
silas.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
silas.importance: The letter names Silvanus in the opening line with Paul and Timothy. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
silas.connections: The letter names him first after Paul. Timothy follows him.

timothy.name: Timothy
timothy.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Silvanus
timothy.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
timothy.importance: The letter names Timothy in the opening line with Paul and Silvanus. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
timothy.connections: The letter names him last, after Paul and Silvanus.

jesus.name: Jesus Christ
jesus.role: Lord who will come, bring relief, and judge
jesus.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesus.importance: Paul says the Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven. He will give relief to the afflicted and punish those who do not obey. Some claim the day of Christ has already come. Paul answers that it has not, and he gives no date.
jesus.connections: Paul calls him the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul links the readers’ calling and comfort with him.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Jesus.”
